transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-14 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Lorenzo (Redwood SE), Priya, Ethan, Sofia (Kestrel)

Summary: quick review of last week's stress pass, discussed anomalies in the 1:20–1:40 window, tuned autoscale cooldown and reserve buffer, agreed on next steps for synthetic 2x burst run and reserved capacity proposal.

[00:00] Maya Chen: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll do the usual check-in, quick data review, then tuning recs and next steps. i see priya and team, great.
[00:22] Priya Nair: yep morning, thanks maya. we got the stress run results, some interesting spikes around tokenization, not sure if that's model or infra.
[00:35] Lorenzo Park: i pulled the traces — there's a brief latency tail at 1:20 where the kv cash warmed up slowly, so the KV cache was cold on a few pods, also we saw a few evictions when the reserve buffer hit threshold.
[01:05] Ethan Morales: yeah i saw evictions too — we set the eviction policy low to test reclaiming but those evictions correlated with a set of 10k concurrent requests in a 3 minute window.
[01:30] Maya Chen: right, that matches our runbook where if reserve hits 85% it starts evicting. for dedicated, the sizing rec is to leave 20-25% headroom for a 2x short burst window. that traded off cost vs safety.
[02:05] Sofia Diaz: can you repeat the 20-25% headroom bit? our finance team will want a concrete number.
[02:15] Maya Chen: sure — so if your long-run steady-state needs 100 rps of model tokens, we recommend reserving for 125 rps equivalent capacity (that's the 25% headroom). that gives autoscaler room to spin up extra capacity without immediate evictions.
[02:50] Priya Nair: whats the recommended autoscale cooldown? we saw a flurry of add/remove events in the logs that looked noisy.
[03:05] Lorenzo Park: we suggest a 90s add cooldown and 5m stable scale down window for workloads with burstiness like yours. shorter cooldown causes jitter, longer delays increases cost.
[03:30] Ethan Morales: does that interact badly with cache warmup? like if new instances spin up, they'll need kv warmup and cold starts add latency.
[03:45] Lorenzo Park: yep — warmup is the hard part. we have a warmup playbook that does a prefix-warmup of frequent prompt shapes and primes the KV cache. i'll drop the scripts. also we recommend pre-warming a small standing buffer (the reserve) so the autoscaler rarely needs to scale from zero.
[04:10] Speaker 1: (murmur) and quantization — we use int8 on some variants, right?
[04:18] Maya Chen: yes, you can use quantized variants for cost saving but remember inference latency sometimes worsens slightly depending on kernel selection. the runtime will pick optimized kernels but quantization + long sequences can be tricky.
[04:40] Priya Nair: on security side, sofia wanted to confirm the V P C peering path and KMS key usage — we need to show this to compliance next week.
[04:55] Sofia Diaz: correct, SOC two docs too. also any traffic egress from your side? we need full flow diagram.
[05:10] Maya Chen: absolutely — we'll share the SOC 2 pack and the private deployment network diagram. redwood private's control plane can be customer-managed with KMS/HSM integrations and we support customer KMS keys for model storage encryption.
[05:35] Ethan Morales: small nit: last time the console showed token-level cost spikes around prompt preamble — is that expected?
[05:48] Lorenzo Park: yes, token-level cost is higher when you do repeated long preambles. our optimize tool suggests caching repeated prefixes and using structured prompts to reduce prefix tokens. also we can recommend a batching window that balances latency.
[06:12] Priya Nair: on fallback plan — if dedicated reserve is exhausted, what's default? do you fall back to hosted model endpoints?
[06:22] Maya Chen: we can configure a fallback policy: route to a compatible hosted model variant (lower-cost or slightly smaller) or spill to a lower tier in the same region. you can also set hard vs soft fail: hard would reject, soft would fallback.
[06:40] Sofia Diaz: do we get an audit trail for those fallback events? we'll need that for incident postmortems.
[06:48] Lorenzo Park: yes — the console records route decisions, model variant, and token counts; it's queryable via the API and included in the audit logs.
[07:05] Ethan Morales: re: canary — how do we run a safe canary? we want to route 10% traffic to reserve-backed instance and monitor p99 latency and cost delta.
[07:18] Maya Chen: typical pattern: start with 5%, run for 24h with synthetic and real traffic probes, watch p50/p95/p99 and error rate, then ramp to 10% if green. we'll support auto-fallback if latency spikes beyond your threshold.
[07:45] Priya Nair: last week's anomaly — the 1:20 tail — any root cause?
[07:52] Lorenzo Park: looking at the traces, a combination of KV cache cold starts and a short spike in gRPC queueing from the orchestration layer. i suspect one pod hit long GC in python runtime on the adapter side — noisy neighbor.
[08:20] Maya Chen: mitigation: set a reserve buffer of at least two warm instances per shard and increase eviction threshold to 92% for this workload, plus the cooldown changes i mentioned. that should blunt the tail.
[08:45] Ethan Morales: can we see simulated numbers if we apply those changes? like expected p99 improvement?
[08:54] Lorenzo Park: yes — i ran a quick sim during prep: with +25% reserve and 90s add cooldown, p99 reduces by ~30-40ms in our model. i'll share the simulation sheet.
[09:15] Priya Nair: cost impact? we need delta to present to finance.
[09:22] Maya Chen: high-level: approx +12-18% monthly on unit costs for the extra reserve buffer; exact depends on commit term and GPU class. we'll put exact numbers in the proposal.
[09:40] Sofia Diaz: any other operational risks? what about burst longer than 3 minutes?
[09:50] Lorenzo Park: for multi-minute sustained bursts, autoscale will add nodes but if burst is long you'll consume reserve and then scale. for that reason we recommend a burst policy that allows temporary overage to a shared spare pool (burst capacity) or configuring a higher reserve commit.
[10:12] Ethan Morales: is there a way to ramp up faster for known events? we have nightly ETL jobs that cause predictable spikes.
[10:22] Maya Chen: yes — schedule-based scaling or pre-provisioning before the ETL run. you can use the console to schedule capacity or trigger a pre-warm hook via API.
[10:35] Priya Nair: let's talk timeline — finance needs decision by 4/27. can you get a draft proposal by 4/20?
[10:42] Maya Chen: yes, i'll send the draft on 4/20.
[10:47] Lorenzo Park: i'll push warmup scripts and sim sheet to the drive link: https://drive.redwood.io/kestrel/poc/warmup (note: link for chat only).
[11:00] Sofia Diaz: for firewall rules i'll send our CIDR ranges, need you to confirm public IPs for peering.
[11:08] Priya Nair: one more quick question — fallback latency: if we route to smaller hosted variant, p99 jumps by how much?
[11:15] Lorenzo Park: depends on model size; for our test, fallback to the t-4 variant increased p99 by ~120-160ms but cost dropped ~30%. tradeoff.
[11:35] Maya Chen: ok wrapping up — recap of next steps: reserved proposal (Maya), warmup playbook (Lorenzo), 2x burst run and telemetry (Ethan), firewall/CIDR confirm (Sofia). schedule canary after reserve is agreed.
[11:55] Priya Nair: sounds good. thanks all.
[12:00] Maya Chen: thanks team — we'll follow up in slack and i'll post the proposal and a short readout doc.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings ("kv cash" vs KV cache), speaker labels may be approximate. references: draft proposal link placeholder, warmup scripts link placeholder.
